plain_english: The light-formed Siva-tattva has been told; but when it cannot enter the undivided mandala, seeing the greater power of autonomy alone, it experiences the non-conceptual immersion of Bhairava. This is his teaching: all this mass of states is a reflection in the sky of knowing — since reflection is marked by appearing in difference, unable to stand alone, shining only by mixture with another. The mark of reflection: a face in a mirror, taste in teeth-water, smell in nostrils, a paired touch in the bliss-organ, a spear-and-pitchfork touch in the inner touch-organ, an echo in the sky.
sanskrit_cite: yad etat prakāśarūpaṃ śivatattvam uktam tatra akhaṇḍamaṇḍale yadā praveṣṭuṃ na śaknoti tadā svātantryaśaktim eva adhikāṃ paśyan nirvikalpam eva bhairavasamāveśam anubhavati ayaṃ ca asya upadeśaḥ sarvam idaṃ bhāvajātaṃ bodhagagane pratibimbamātraṃ pratibimbalakṣaṇopetatvāt idaṃ hi pratibimbasya lakṣaṇaṃ yat bhedena bhāsitam aśaktam anyavyāmiśratvenaiva bhāti tat pratibimbam mukharūpam iva darpaṇe rasa iva dantodake gandha iva ghrāṇa mithunasparśa iva ānandendriye śūlakuntādisparśo vā antaḥsparśanendriye pratiśrutkeva vyomni

plain_english: That taste is not primary, because its works — curing disease and the rest — proceed by an occult eye.
sanskrit_cite: na hi sa raso mukhyaḥ tatkāryavyādhiśamanādyadṛṣṭeḥ

plain_english: Nor are smell and touch primary: they belong to qualities, and in the qualitied's absence they cannot be, since the effect-chain begins without them.
sanskrit_cite: nāpi gandhasparśau mukhyau guṇinaḥ tatra abhāve tayor ayogāt kāryaparamparānārambhāt ca

plain_english: And they are not simply nonexistent either — as body-stripping, seed, and the rest show.
sanskrit_cite: na ca tau na staḥ dehoddhūlanavisargādidarśanāt

plain_english: Sound too is not primary: someone speaks it, and it is heard like an echo of one arriving.
sanskrit_cite: śabdo 'pi na mukhyaḥ ko 'pi vakti iti āgacchantyā iva pratiśrutkāyāḥ śravaṇāt

plain_english: As that reflected thing shines, so the world shines in the light of the Supreme Lord.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yathā etat pratibimbitaṃ bhāti tathaiva viśvaṃ parameśvaraprakāśe

plain_english: But what would the image here be? Let it not be anything at all.
sanskrit_cite: nanu atra bimbaṃ kiṃ syāt mābhūt kiṃcit

plain_english: How is that causeless? Then comes the question of the reason: why? By the logic of mirror-speech the reason will be the Supreme Lord's power itself — the synonym of autonomy. And because it bears the world's reflection, the Lord's world-selfhood follows: consciousness-made is the world, the place where consciousness manifests — this world here is obstruction, reflection-bearing. But that world-selfhood is the Lord's own nature, not un-contradicted, since self-nature contemplation of consciousness-nature cannot be.
sanskrit_cite: nanu kim akāraṇakaṃ tat hanta tarhi hetupraśnaḥ tat kiṃ bimbavācoyuktyā hetuś ca parameśvaraśaktir eva svātantryāparaparyāyā bhaviṣyati viśvapratibimbadhāritvāc ca viśvātmakatvaṃ bhagavataḥ saṃvinmayaṃ hi viśvaṃ caitanyasya vyaktisthānam iti tad eva hi viśvam atra pratīpam iti pratibimbadhāritvam asya tac ca tāvat viśvātmakatvaṃ parameśvarasya svarūpaṃ na anāmṛṣṭaṃ bhavati citsvabhāvasya svarūpānāmarśanānupapatteḥ

plain_english: For in contemplation of the self's own nature there would in reality be mere inertness; and this contemplation does not depend on another — it is inseparable from consciousness-nature alone, the womb of supreme sound, so declared: as much as he is the Lord's world-establishing group of powers, so much does he contemplate.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpānāmarśane hi vastuto jaḍataiva syāt āmarśaś ca ayaṃ na sāketikaḥ api tu citsvabhāvatāmātranāntarīyakaḥ paranādagarbha uktaḥ sa ca yāvān viśvavyavasthāpakaḥ parameśvarasya śaktikalāpaḥ tāvantam āmṛśati

plain_english: There the three primary powers of the Supreme Lord are unsurpassable-will-awakening — that very triad is a i u. From this triad the whole play of powers is carried. In the unsurpassable, rest is bliss; rest in will is rulership; awakening's rest is the wave. The beginning of action-power is that triad ā ī ū.
sanskrit_cite: tatra mukhyās tāvat tisraḥ parameśvarasya śaktayaḥ anuttarecchonmeṣa iti tad eva parāmarśatrayam a i u iti etasmād eva tritayāt sarvaḥ śaktiprapañcaḥ caryate anuttara eva hi viśrāntir ānandaḥ icchāyām eva viśrāntiḥ īśanam unmeṣa eva hi viśrāntir ūrmiḥ yaḥ kriyāśakteḥ prārambhaḥ tad eva parāmarśatrayam ā ī ū iti

plain_english: There the prior triad of contemplations, being the essence of the light-part, is sun-natured; the final triad, by the prevalence of rest-natured bliss, is moon-natured — up to where the entry of the action-portion does not reach.
sanskrit_cite: atra ca prācyaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ prakāśabhāgasāratvāt sūryātmakaṃ caramaṃ parāmarśatrayaṃ viśrāntisvabhāvāhlādaprādhānyāt somātmakam iyati yāvat karmāṃśasya anupraveśo nāsti

plain_english: When action enters will and rulership, what is entered and ruled is called iṣyamāṇa and īśyamāṇa. It has two kinds: by mere light, ra-utterance; by rest, la-utterance — ra and la being light-and-stopping in nature. And the willed is not distinct like the external — in distinctness would lie its own creation; nor is will or rulership distinct — from non-distinctness only hearing stands for ra and la, no stable expression.
sanskrit_cite: yadā tu icchāyām īśane ca karma anupraviśati yat tat iṣyamāṇam īśyamāṇam iti ca ucyate tadā asya dvau bhedau prakāśamātreṇa raśrutiḥ viśrāntyā laśrutiḥ ralayoḥ prakāśastambhasvabhāvatvāt iṣyamāṇaṃ ca na bāhyavat sphuṭam sphuṭarūpatve tad eva nirmāṇaṃ syāt na icchā īśanaṃ vā ataḥ asphuṭatvāt eva śrutimātraṃ ralayoḥ na vyañjanavat sthitiḥ

plain_english: This quad of letters is neuter, because it bears both shades: ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ.
sanskrit_cite: tad etad varṇacatuṣṭayam ubhayacchāyādhāritvāt napuṃsakam ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ iti

plain_english: When the spread of unsurpassable-bliss runs in will and the rest, the letter-pair is e and oṃ.
sanskrit_cite: anuttarānandayoḥ icchādiṣu yadā prasaraḥ tadā varṇadvayam e oṃ iti

plain_english: Further still, from the union of unsurpassable-bliss, the pair ai and au.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi punar anuttarānandasaṃghaṭṭāt varṇadvayam ai au iti

plain_english: This is action-power — and that very quad is e ai o au.
sanskrit_cite: sā iyaṃ kriyāśaktiḥ tad eva ca varṇacatuṣṭayam e ai o au iti

plain_english: Then at the end of action-power everything stands as effect; as far as it will enter the unsurpassable, just so long the prior stands as the essence of consciousness, as mere light, as the point: am.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ punaḥ kriyāśaktyante sarvaṃ kāryabhūtaṃ yāvat anuttare pravekṣyati tāvad eva pūrvaṃ saṃvedanasāratayā prakāśamātratvena bindutayā āste am iti

plain_english: Then from that very place the visarga of the unsurpassable is born: aḥ.
sanskrit_cite: tatas tatraiva anuttarasya visargo jāyate aḥ iti

plain_english: Thus the sixteenfold seed-form of the contemplations is declared.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ parāmarśānāṃ bījasvarūpam ucyate

plain_english: Born from them, expression-natured, the womb-form.
sanskrit_cite: tadutthaṃ vyañjanātmakaṃ yonirūpam

plain_english: There from the unsurpassable comes the ka-class — of faith; the ca-class — of object-bearing will; the pair ṭa- and ta-classes — from awakening; the pa-class — from union with the five powers; hence fivefoldness.
sanskrit_cite: tatra anuttarāt kavargaḥ śraddhāyāḥ icchāyāḥ cavargaḥ sakarmikāyā icchāyā dvau ṭavargas tavargaś ca unmeṣāt pavargaḥ śaktipañcakayogāt pañcakatvam

plain_english: Of threefold will, ya ra lā come from awakening, and the va-letter; of threefold will, śa ṣa sā come from the visarga, and the ha-letter; the kṣa-letter is born of the womb-union.
sanskrit_cite: icchāyā eva trividhāyā ya ra lāḥ unmeṣāt vakāraḥ icchāyā eva trividhāyāḥ śa ṣa sāḥ visargāt hakāraḥ yonisaṃyogajaḥ kṣakāraḥ

plain_english: Thus this Lord is the unsurpassable himself, in the form of the clan-Lord.
sanskrit_cite: ity eva eṣa bhagavān anuttara eva kuleśvararūpaḥ

plain_english: His is one kaulic power of visarga, by which, from bliss-form onward to the end of outward creation, throbbing, the class-contemplations and the rest outward have attained the form of tattvas.
sanskrit_cite: tasya ca ekaiva kaulikī visargaśaktiḥ yayā ānandarūpāt prabhṛti iyatā bahiḥsṛṣṭiparyantena praspandataḥ vargādiparāmarśā eva bahis tattvarūpatāṃ prāptāḥ

plain_english: That visarga is threefold: āṇava, the form of mind's rest; śākta, marked by mind's awakening; śāṃbhava, the form of mind's dissolution.
sanskrit_cite: sa ca eṣa visargas tridhā āṇavaḥ cittaviśrāntirūpaḥ śāktaḥ cittasaṃbodhalakṣaṇaḥ śāṃbhavaḥ cittapralayarūpaḥ iti

plain_english: Thus the visarga itself is the Lord's power in the birth of the world.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ visarga eva viśvajanane bhagavataḥ śaktiḥ

plain_english: When contemplation is by undividedness alone, then the Lord is one as the seed-womb — part-wise in contemplation, the power-endowed and the power.
sanskrit_cite: ity evam iyato yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca

plain_english: Separate in the eightfold contemplation, in union with the wheel-Lord, nine classes; in the prevalence of each single contemplation, fiftyfold.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthak aṣṭakaparāmarśe cakreśvarasāhityena navavargaḥ ekaikaparāmarśaprādhānye pañcāśadātmakatā

plain_english: Even there, in contemplation of a possibly differing part, eightyfold.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi sambhavadbhāgabhedaparāmarśane ekāśītirūpatvam

plain_english: In reality there are only six contemplations; by spreading and returning, twelve — they nourish the fullness of the Supreme Lord's world-power.
sanskrit_cite: vastutas tu ṣaṭ eva parāmarśāḥ prasaraṇapratisaṃcaraṇayogena dvādaśa bhavantaḥ parameśvarasya viśvaśaktipūrṇatvaṃ puṣṇanti

plain_english: Those very powers, being contemplation-formed, are the Lord's — Śrīkālikā they are named.
sanskrit_cite: tā eva etāḥ parāmarśarūpatvāt śaktayo bhagavatyaḥ śrīkālikā iti niruktāḥ

plain_english: These too, pure contemplations that are power-formed, in pure knowledge by the para-apara form, from the mere contraction of māyā's awakening, share the nature of the knower and the known.
sanskrit_cite: ete ca śaktirūpā eva śuddhāḥ parāmarśāḥ śuddhavidyāyāṃ parāpararūpatvena māyonmeṣamātrasaṃkocāt vidyāvidyeśvararūpatāṃ bhajante

plain_english: In māyā again, the crystal-clear divisions take māyic letter-nature — those who, attaining mundanity in paśyantī, madhyamā and vaikharī, stand up to the nature of external tattvas. When they are seen as body-like and revived by those pure contemplations — the life-replacing ones — they become vigorous, granting enjoyment and liberation. Thus, seeing oneself as merely the rest of all contemplations, as the reflection of all tattva-being-world divisions, by non-conceptuality, by the immersion of śāṃbhava — liberated while living.
sanskrit_cite: māyāyāṃ punaḥ sphaṭībhūtabhedavibhāgā māyīyavarṇatāṃ bhajante ye paśyantīmadhyamāvaikharīṣu vyāvahārikatvam āsādya bahīrūpatattvasvabhāvatāpattiparyantāḥ te ca māyīyā api śarīrakalpatvena yadā dṛśyante yadā ca teṣām uktanayair etaiḥ jīvitasthānīyaiḥ śuddhaiḥ parāmarśaiḥ pratyujjīvanaṃ kriyate tadā te savīryā bhavanti te ca tādṛśā bhogamokṣapradāḥ ity evaṃ sakalaparāmarśaviśrāntimātrarūpaṃ pratibimbitasamastatattvabhūtabhuvanabhedam ātmānaṃ paśyato nirvikalpatayā śāṃbhavena samāveśena jīvanmuktatā

plain_english: Even here, as before, there is no obstruction of mantra and the like.
sanskrit_cite: atrāpi pūrvavat na mantrādiyantraṇā kācid iti
